ST-020.heroHeading: Furnace help for life at home.
ST-020.heroBody: The house feels cold, the furnace sounds different, or you are planning a change. Find the repair, replacement, or care path that fits what is happening.
ST-020.label: Ask about furnace help
ST-020.preparationBody: Choose the concern closest to yours. You do not have to diagnose the problem first.

preparation.title: What you notice
preparation.body: Tell us whether heat stopped, a room stays cold or you want to plan ahead. The equipment type, controls and past work can help guide the right assessment.

preparation.title: What you want to change
preparation.body: If something stopped, ask about a diagnosis. If the system works but you are planning ahead, compare care or replacement options based on the home’s needs.

preparation.title: Before a visit
preparation.body: Share what you want checked or changed, the equipment if known and any current problem. Confirm whether your address and requested work can be served, what the visit covers, any charges and current availability. A request is not an appointment; the visit needs a separate confirmation.

ST-020.findingsHeading: What to check before choosing furnace work.
ST-020.processHeading: A clear next step. More room for home life.
ST-020.processBody: Start with the concern, agree on the work, and understand the finish.
steps: Choose the right conversation.
Share the equipment and what you notice or want to change. Confirm the visit scope, charge, and available appointment.
Decide with the findings in view.
Review the recommended work, what it would address, its full cost, and anything still unknown before approving it.
Make room for the rest of your day.
After the agreed work, review the checks and any remaining next step. Keep the record and get back to the moments you enjoy at home.
ST-020.closeHeading: Let’s give your furnace question a clear next step.
ST-020.closeBody: Bring the concern or the change you are planning. Ask about the help that fits, so you can make the choice with useful information.
ST-020.safety: Gas smell? Leave. From a safe place, call 911 and your gas utility. Do not use switches or try to relight the furnace. Suspected carbon monoxide? Get outside to fresh air and call 911. Smoke or immediate danger? Leave and call 911 from a safe place.
ST-020.quoteIntro: Each path answers a different question.

servicePaths.body: Maintenance is a defined check and care visit. It is not every repair the furnace might need.

ST-077.heroHeading: Understand the air concern before choosing a product.
ST-077.heroBody: Want to understand a recurring air concern before buying a device? Ask what the assessment can check, what it cannot tell you, and which question it can help answer.
ST-077.label: Ask about air quality assessment
ST-077.preparationHeading: Start with the air concern in your home.
ST-077.preparationBody: Where it happens and when it changes help frame the right question.

preparation.title: The concern and its pattern
preparation.body: A pattern can help choose useful observations. Ask how the duration, locations and conditions of any measurement affect its meaning.

preparation.title: What you want to understand
preparation.body: Share the affected rooms, timing, and anything that changed. Keep observations separate from a confirmed cause.

preparation.title: The requested visit
preparation.body: Share what you want checked or changed, the equipment if known and any current problem. Confirm whether your address and requested work can be served, what the visit covers, any charges and current availability. A request is not an appointment; the visit needs a separate confirmation.

ST-077.findingsHeading: Understand the measurement before choosing the next check.
ST-077.processHeading: From an air concern to an informed choice.
ST-077.processBody: Name the question, understand the limits, and choose supported work.
steps: Agree on the question.
Share the concern and the rooms involved. Confirm the visit scope, what can be checked, and the charge.
Choose within the findings.
Review what the observations establish and what they leave unknown. Get the proposed work, full cost, and limits clear before approval.
Review the findings and next question.
After the agreed assessment, review the observations, what they establish, and what remains unknown. Choose any next check or work separately, then get back to the rest of your day.
ST-077.closeHeading: Let’s make your air-quality question clearer.
ST-077.closeBody: You do not need to choose a device before understanding the concern. Ask about the next check or product comparison for your home.
ST-077.quoteHeading: What the proposed work should explain.
ST-077.quoteIntro: A measured result, a possible source, and a product claim are different things.

quoteQuestions.title: The question and the limits
quoteQuestions.body: What does this assessment or product address, and what can it not establish?

quoteQuestions.title: The home and equipment fit
quoteQuestions.body: How do the rooms, airflow, existing equipment, and proposed settings affect the recommendation?

quoteQuestions.title: Full cost and ongoing care
quoteQuestions.body: What is the full charge? What filters, supplies, and care will cost extra later?

quoteQuestions.title: Checks and next steps
quoteQuestions.body: What will be checked after the agreed work, and what remains unknown? Approve additional work separately.

ST-077.quoteLimit: Air-cleaning products are not a medical diagnosis or treatment. Ask what the findings support before choosing the work.
